facts.name: Strawflower
facts.color: Yellow, orange, red, pink or white papery flowers (yellow shown)
facts.notes: Papery, crinkly flowers that keep their color fresh or dried, from midsummer until frost. An annual: plant after the last frost in late May. Cut flowers just as they start to open for drying; taller kinds may need a stake.

sources.title: Garden Hoard (Renegade Acres, Howell, MI): Strawflower 'Tall Double Mix' seeds
sources.note: Xerochrysum bracteatum seed grown and sold by a farm in Howell, Michigan.

sources.title: Illinois Extension: Plant of the week, Strawflower
sources.note: Grows in average, dry to medium, well-drained soil in full sun and takes a little light shade. Start seed indoors 6 to 8 weeks before the last frost and plant out after. Lasts well cut and keeps its color dried.

sources.title: Utah State University Extension: Strawflower Cut Flower Production
sources.note: Full-sun annual with papery bracts up to 2 inches across on plants up to 42 inches tall; does well with little water.

sources.title: Rutgers NJAES: Landscape Plants Rated by Deer Resistance (printable list)
sources.note: Annuals: calendula and strawflower are rated A (rarely damaged); California poppy, verbena and zinnia B (seldom severely damaged); cosmos C (occasionally severely damaged).

companions.why: Plant strawflower with zinnias, basil, marigolds, sweet William and flax.

sources.title: Epic Gardening: How to Plant, Grow, and Care for Strawflowers
